summary.text: A male patient presented with headache for 2 months that was worsening, a progressively increasing right frontal skull swelling for one month and occasional fever, without known trauma, weight loss or past tuberculosis. He was staying in a hostel with a friend who was taking anti-tuberculous therapy, was a non-smoker and a social drinker.

Examination showed a soft, non-tender 5cm x 4cm swelling on the right forehead with normal local temperature, normal power, intact sensation and cranial nerves, and no meningeal irritation. Routine investigations and chest x-ray were normal. Head CT showed erosion of the right frontal bone with a lentiform extra-axial collection and scalp soft tissue swelling, read as likely osteomyelitis.

He was admitted for surgical removal of the epidural and subgaleal collections and started on intravenous ceftriaxone, metronidazole and amikacin. At surgery about 20 ml of frank pus was found beneath the skin, the underlying bone was soft and porous, and a burr hole showed epidural pus; the pus was drained and sent for culture and the inflamed pericranium for histopathology. Intravenous antibiotics were continued and he recovered well after the operation.

Histopathology showed well-formed granulomas with caseous necrosis and bony fragments, with acid-fast bacilli consistent with tuberculosis, and Category I anti-tuberculous therapy was started. On follow up the symptoms had subsided, the patient was well at the time of writing and had completed the course of therapy, and head CT on follow up after 1 month showed complete resolution of the abscess.
